AngularJS vs Angular?

AngularJS (1.x) is JavaScript, MVC with $scope, two-way digest cycles, and is end-of-life. Angular (2+) is TypeScript, component-based, has hierarchical DI, AOT compilation, RxJS, a CLI, and is much faster.
What are standalone components? NgModule vs standalone?

Since v14 (ng new generates them from v17; standalone: true is the default from v19), components can declare their own dependencies with imports: [] instead of being declared in an NgModule. You bootstrap with bootstrapApplication(App, { providers: [provideRouter(routes), provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([...]))] }). This means less boilerplate and better tree-shaking.
Types of data binding?

Interpolation {{ }} and property binding [ ] go from component to view. Event binding ( ) goes from view to component. Two-way binding [( )] is the "banana in a box", e.g. [(ngModel)], or model() signals in v17+.
Directives: component vs structural vs attribute?

Component: a directive with a template. Structural: changes the DOM layout (*ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch, now the built-in @if / @for / @switch control flow). Attribute: changes appearance or behavior (ngClass, ngStyle, or custom ones using @HostListener and @HostBinding).
Pure vs impure pipes?

A pure pipe (the default) re-runs only when its input reference changes, so it's fast. An impure pipe (pure: false) runs on every change detection cycle; async is impure. Built-in pipes: date, currency, uppercase, json, async, slice, percent.
How does Dependency Injection work in Angular?

DI is hierarchical: the environment injector (root or route) sits above element injectors (component providers). providedIn: 'root' creates a tree-shakable singleton. Providers at component level give a new instance for that subtree. Inject with the constructor or inject(). Provider types: useClass, useValue, useFactory, useExisting. Use InjectionToken for non-class values.
How do components communicate?

- Parent → child: @Input() / input() signal
- Child → parent: @Output() EventEmitter / output()
- Parent reads child: @ViewChild / viewChild()
- Unrelated components: a shared service holding a BehaviorSubject or signal
- App-wide state: NgRx / Signal Store
- Through the router: params and query params
Observable vs Promise?

Observable (RxJS) | Promise
Can emit many values over time | Resolves once
Lazy: nothing happens until subscribed | Eager: starts immediately
Cancellable (unsubscribe) | Can't be cancelled
Rich operators (map, filter, debounce, retry) | then/catch only
Subject vs BehaviorSubject vs ReplaySubject vs AsyncSubject?

Subject: no initial value; late subscribers miss earlier emissions. BehaviorSubject: needs an initial value and gives the latest value to new subscribers (good for state). ReplaySubject(n): replays the last n values. AsyncSubject: emits only the last value, on complete.
switchMap vs mergeMap vs concatMap vs exhaustMap?

- switchMap: cancels the previous inner observable (search typeahead).
- mergeMap: runs all of them in parallel (independent saves).
- concatMap: runs them one at a time, in order (queued writes).
- exhaustMap: ignores new values while one is running (a login button clicked repeatedly).
this.search.valueChanges.pipe(
  debounceTime(300), distinctUntilChanged(),
  switchMap(q => this.api.search(q))
).subscribe(r => this.results = r);
How do you avoid memory leaks with subscriptions?
Use the async pipe (it unsubscribes automatically) · takeUntilDestroyed() (v16+) · toSignal() · take(1) · or call unsubscribe() in ngOnDestroy. HttpClient observables complete by themselves.
What are Signals? Signals vs RxJS?

Signals (v16+) are reactive values: signal() is writable, computed() is derived and memoized, and effect() runs side effects. They're synchronous and always have a current value, and they let Angular update only what changed, which opens the way to zoneless change detection. Use signals for UI state. Keep RxJS for async event streams (HTTP, websockets, debouncing). toSignal and toObservable bridge the two.
How does change detection work? What is OnPush?

Zone.js patches async APIs (events, timers, XHR), and after each one Angular checks the component tree from the top down. With OnPush, a component is checked only when an @Input reference changes, an event fires inside it, the async pipe emits, a signal it reads changes, or you call markForCheck(). Use immutable data with OnPush. Zoneless started as experimental in v18 (provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()) and became stable in v20.2 as provideZonelessChangeDetection().
Template-driven vs Reactive forms?
Routing: guards, resolvers, lazy loading?

Guards (functional since v15): canActivate, canActivateChild, canDeactivate (unsaved changes), canMatch (choose between routes). A resolver fetches data before the route activates. Lazy loading with loadComponent / loadChildren splits bundles and shrinks the initial load. @defer blocks (v17) lazy-load parts of a template.
What is an HTTP Interceptor? Uses?

Middleware that sits around every HttpClient request and response. Uses: attaching the JWT, global error handling (401 → redirect to login or refresh the token), a loading spinner, logging, caching, retries.
AOT vs JIT?

AOT (the default) compiles templates at build time: a smaller bundle, faster rendering, template errors caught early, and better security. JIT compiles in the browser at runtime; it was the old dev mode.
ViewChild vs ContentChild; ng-content?

@ViewChild queries elements in the component's own template (available in ngAfterViewInit). @ContentChild queries projected content passed between the component's tags with <ng-content> (available in ngAfterContentInit). <ng-content select=".header"> enables multi-slot projection.
How do you optimize Angular performance?

OnPush or signals · track in @for (trackBy) · lazy routes and @defer · pure pipes instead of methods in templates · virtual scrolling (CDK) · unsubscribing · SSR and hydration (@angular/ssr) · image optimization (NgOptimizedImage) · bundle budgets · esbuild builder.
ng-template vs ng-container vs ng-content?

<ng-template>: a template that isn't rendered until it's used (via ngTemplateOutlet or else blocks). <ng-container>: a grouping element that adds no DOM node. <ng-content>: the slot for content projection.

RxJS output: retry, finalize and teardown order

const { defer, of, throwError, retry, tap, finalize, map, catchError, Observable, timer } = require('rxjs');
let attempts = 0;
defer(() => { attempts++; console.log('attempt', attempts); return attempts < 3 ? throwError(() => new Error('fail')) : of('data'); }).pipe(
  retry({ count: 2, delay: () => timer(1) }),
  finalize(() => console.log('finalize')),
).subscribe({ next: console.log, complete: () => console.log('complete') });
Output (executed):
attempt 1
attempt 2
attempt 3
data
complete
finalize
retry re-subscribes to the source, so a cold HTTP observable sends a new request each time. The object form accepts a delay function for backoff. count: 2 means two retries, three attempts in all. finalize runs on completion, error or unsubscribe, after complete, making it the right place to stop a loading spinner.

Walk through what happens when a user clicks a button in a zone-based Default app.

- The browser dispatches the event, and zone.js's patched listener runs inside the Angular zone.
- Your handler runs and updates state.
- When the task's stack empties, NgZone.onMicrotaskEmpty fires, and ApplicationRef.tick() runs.
- Angular walks the tree from the root, re-evaluates bindings, and writes changed values to the DOM.
- In dev mode, a second pass verifies that no binding changed.
A child with OnPush doesn't refresh after the parent does this.user.name = 'New'. Why? What are the fixes?

The reference held by [user] is unchanged, so Object.is reports no change and the child stays clean. Fixes, best first: hold the data in a signal and update it with a new object; or assign a new object with this.user = { ...this.user, name: 'New' }. Calling markForCheck() in the child works but hides the mutation.
markForCheck() vs detectChanges()?

markForCheck() flags this view and all ancestors so the next tick visits them. It does not run anything itself, and it is what you use with OnPush after a change arrives from outside, such as a WebSocket callback. detectChanges() runs a check right now on this view and its children, and can be used when the view is detached. Calling it from a parent's hook during a check can throw or cause extra work.
What happens to zone-based code after moving to zoneless?

Anything that updated a plain field in a setTimeout, promise or third-party callback and relied on a global tick stops refreshing the view. Components must notify Angular through signals, markForCheck (or the async pipe), or template events. Also remove zone.js from the polyfills build option, and replace code using NgZone.onMicrotaskEmpty or onStable with afterNextRender. Tests that use fakeAsync depend on zone.js, so need to be changed. Converting components to OnPush first is the usual migration path, as OnPush code is close to zoneless-ready.
computed vs effect vs linkedSignal: which would you use to reset a selection when a list changes?

linkedSignal. The selection is writable by the user but must reset or re-derive when the source changes. A computed is read-only, so the user could not change it. An effect that calls selected.set(...) works but runs later than the render that needs the value, which causes an extra pass and a moment of inconsistent state. Treat "effect that writes a signal" as a warning sign.
Why might an effect not re-run? Why might it loop?

It tracks only signals read synchronously in its last run. If a read sits after an await or inside a setTimeout, or an early return skipped it, there is no dependency. It also does not re-run when a signal is set to an equal value. It loops when it reads and writes the same signal. Fix by wrapping the read in untracked(), or preferably by replacing the effect with computed.
Signals vs RxJS: when would you still pick RxJS?

A signal holds a current value; an observable describes values over time. Signals drop intermediate writes: setting a signal twice in one task means a template or effect sees only the last. So they cannot model events you must not miss. Use RxJS for debouncing, retry, cancellation, combining streams, and WebSockets. A common pattern is RxJS for the async pipeline, and toSignal at the end, so that the template reads a signal.
providers vs viewProviders?

Both create an instance per component. providers are visible to the component, its view children and to content projected into it. viewProviders are hidden from projected content. So content passed in through ng-content gets the outer value, which prevents a library component's internals from leaking into its consumers' content.
useClass vs useExisting vs useValue vs useFactory; what is a multi provider?

useClass creates a new instance of the class. useExisting is an alias pointing to an already provided token, so there is one instance under two tokens. Getting this wrong by using useClass makes two instances. useValue supplies a ready object. useFactory runs a function, which may call inject(). With multi: true, many providers contribute to one token and injection gives an array. Validators (NG_VALIDATORS) and value accessors work this way.
What does NullInjectorError: No provider for X mean, and how do you debug it?

The lookup went through every injector and none had the token. Typical causes: the service has no @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }); provideHttpClient() is missing from the app config; a component is looking for a token provided only in a sibling route; or a test has not provided a dependency. The error shows the chain, such as R3InjectorError(Standalone[App])[A -> B -> C], whose last item is what is missing.
What is forwardRef?

JS classes are not hoisted, so a decorator that refers to a class declared later in the file sees it in its TDZ. forwardRef(() => MyClass) delays the read until it is needed. It is common in NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR providers, since the provider is in the class's own decorator.
canActivate vs canMatch: which stops a lazy bundle from downloading?

canMatch. It runs while matching, before the lazy code is loaded. If it returns false, the router moves on to the next matching route, so you can have two path: 'dashboard' entries for admin and user. canActivate runs after matching. Remember that hiding a bundle is not security, since all JS is public.
Resolver vs loading in the component: which is better?

A resolver delays navigation until data arrives, so the page shows complete data, but the user sees nothing happen while waiting, and a failed resolve cancels navigation. Loading in the component navigates immediately and shows a skeleton, which feels faster and lets you handle errors in place. Most modern apps prefer the second approach, keeping resolvers for data that the page cannot render without.
Why does the same component not re-initialise on /orders/1 to /orders/2?

The router's default RouteReuseStrategy reuses a component when the route config is the same. So constructor and ngOnInit do not run again. Read the id reactively: route.paramMap.pipe(switchMap(...)), or a signal input with withComponentInputBinding(), feeding a resource or computed.
value vs getRawValue(); setValue vs patchValue; typed form pitfalls?

value omits disabled controls, and so in typed forms each field's type includes undefined. getRawValue() includes them. setValue demands every key and patchValue takes a subset. Without nonNullable, reset() sets null, so each control's type is T | null. Using NonNullableFormBuilder or fb.nonNullable removes the null. Type inference needs an initial value, so declare an interface for an initially empty FormArray.
How do you build a custom form control?

Implement ControlValueAccessor: writeValue receives a value from the model, registerOnChange(fn) saves the callback that you call when the user changes the value, registerOnTouched(fn) saves the one you call on blur, and setDisabledState handles disabling. Register with NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR using multi: true. For OnPush controls, writeValue is called outside of inputs, so update a signal or call markForCheck. Implementing Validator and registering NG_VALIDATORS adds built-in validation.
Does cancelling HTTP with switchMap stop the backend?

No. Unsubscribing aborts the browser's request, so the response is ignored, but the server may already be processing it. Spring does not normally notice a client disconnect until it writes the response. That is why switchMap suits reads, not writes. For writes use concatMap or exhaustMap, and make the endpoint idempotent, such as with an idempotency key.
Implement a typeahead with error handling and a loading flag.
How would you cache an HTTP result and share one request across components?
Why is calling a method in a template bad? When is it fine?

A method in a binding runs on every check of that view, so an expensive one (sorting, filtering) can run many times per second. Prefer a computed or a pure pipe. Calling a signal is also a function call, but it is a cheap read of a memoized value, so {{ total() }} is fine when total is a signal. With OnPush, or for trivial getters, the cost is usually unimportant.
trackBy/track: what happens without it, and with track $index?

With identity tracking and fresh objects from an API, every item looks new, so the DOM is destroyed and rebuilt, which is slow and loses focus and input state. With track item.id, nodes are kept and reordered. With track $index the node at position n stays and only its bindings change, so stateful content (an input's typed value, an open dropdown) ends up attached to a different item when items are removed or reordered.
ng-container and ngTemplateOutlet: build a reusable table whose cell layout is supplied by the parent.

Accept a template with rowTpl = input.required<TemplateRef<{ $implicit: Row }>>() or find it with contentChild(TemplateRef). Render it with <ng-container *ngTemplateOutlet="rowTpl(); context: { $implicit: r }" />. The parent writes <ng-template let-row>...</ng-template>. Unlike ng-content, this renders the template once per row, and passes data from child to parent's template. A static ngTemplateContextGuard on a directive can give strict typing for let- variables.
ElementRef vs Renderer2: when do you touch the DOM directly?

Bindings come first. When you need imperative work, Renderer2 abstracts the DOM and works under SSR. ElementRef.nativeElement gives the raw element, for example to call focus() or to give a canvas to a chart library, which should sit in afterNextRender. Setting innerHTML directly bypasses Angular's sanitiser, which is an XSS risk. Use the [innerHTML] binding, which sanitises.
How does Angular protect against XSS? What does bypassSecurityTrustHtml do?

Angular treats every bound value as untrusted. Interpolation escapes text. [innerHTML], [href] and [style] pass through contextual sanitising, which removes scripts and javascript: URLs. AOT also means template text is not built from user strings. DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrust* tells Angular to trust a value, so only use it with content you control. Never build templates from user input. HttpClient also supports CSRF: it reads the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and sends the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on same-origin mutating requests.
Explain NgRx in an interview in under a minute. When would you avoid it?

The store holds one state tree. Components dispatch actions that describe events. Pure reducers compute the next state. Selectors read memoized slices. Effects listen for actions, make API calls, and dispatch results. You get predictable flows, time-travel debugging and easy testing. Avoid it for small apps, form state, or data that only one screen uses, because the boilerplate outweighs the benefit. A service with signals, or SignalStore, is often enough.
Why must a reducer be pure? Why are selectors memoized?

A pure reducer takes state and action and returns a new state, with no I/O or mutation. Purity means the same action log always reproduces the same state, which enables time travel and simple tests, and new references let OnPush detect changes by reference. createSelector remembers its last inputs and returns the cached result if those references are unchanged, so derived data is not recomputed and subscribers do not get a new array on every state change.
Scenario: an effect stops working after the first API failure.

The catchError is on the outer actions$ stream, so the error completes the effect's stream. Move catchError inside switchMap, on the API call, and return a failure action. NgRx does resubscribe effects a limited number of times by default, but you should not depend on that.
What is hydration, and what breaks it?

Hydration reuses server-rendered DOM on the client: Angular walks the existing nodes rather than creating new ones, then attaches listeners. It breaks when the client's DOM would differ from the server's: direct DOM manipulation, third-party scripts that alter the markup, invalid HTML that the browser's parser repairs, or a render that depends on Date.now() or Math.random() in the template. CDN settings that strip comment nodes also break it, since Angular relies on them. Check the console for NG05xx messages.
Why might SSR hang or time out?

The server waits until the app is stable, meaning no pending tasks. A setInterval, an open WebSocket, or a long-lived observable keeps it unstable. Move those into afterNextRender, which only runs in the browser, or guard them with isPlatformBrowser. Pending HTTP calls count too, so a slow API delays the response. Give them timeouts.
fakeAsync vs waitForAsync vs real async tests?

fakeAsync runs the test in a fake zone, with virtual time moved by tick() and flush(), so tests of timers and debounce are fast. It cannot deal with real XHR, and it needs zone.js. waitForAsync waits for pending tasks in the zone. Plain async/await with fixture.whenStable() works for both zone and zoneless tests. A runner's fake timers, such as those in Vitest or Jest, are the zoneless replacement for tick.
How do you test a service that uses HttpClient?
Scenario: a big list of 20,000 rows lags on every keystroke in a filter box. How do you diagnose and fix it?

- Profile with Angular DevTools to see which components re-run, and the Performance panel to separate script time from layout.
- Debounce the input.
- Render fewer DOM nodes with CDK virtual scroll or server-side pagination.
- Use OnPush rows with a stable track.
- Compute the filter in a computed, so it runs once per change, and remove function calls from row templates.
- If the filter itself is slow, run it in a Web Worker, or on the server.
Scenario: design the front end of an order dashboard for a large team.

Standalone feature folders with lazy route arrays, one per domain. Each feature has route-scoped stores (SignalStore or signal services) and generated API clients from the Spring OpenAPI document. Shared UI lives in a library, with Storybook if the team needs one. OnPush everywhere, signals for state, RxJS for streams such as live updates over SSE or WebSocket. Interceptors for auth, correlation IDs and error toasts. Budgets and lint rules enforcing boundaries, such as an Nx workspace with module boundaries. Tests: unit for logic, harness-based component tests, a thin Playwright suite for critical flows. Deploy static files behind nginx or a CDN, with runtime config loaded at start-up.
How do you deal with a Spring Boot backend and Angular on different origins in development and production?

In development, use the Angular dev-server proxy so the browser sees one origin, and CORS does not arise. In production, either serve both under one domain (nginx routes /api to Spring), or enable CORS in Spring with an explicit origin list. If cookies are used across sites, you need SameSite=None; Secure and withCredentials: true in HttpClient. Angular's automatic XSRF header is added only to same-origin relative URLs, so a cross-origin API needs its own solution.
What is @defer doing at compile time?

The compiler sees which standalone components, directives and pipes are used only inside a @defer block, and moves them out of the eager imports into dynamic import() calls, creating a separate chunk. At run time, the trigger loads that chunk and then renders the block. If a dependency is referenced by a viewChild query or elsewhere in the same template outside the block, it stays eager, and @defer silently saves nothing.
EventEmitter vs Subject; can a service use output()?

EventEmitter extends Subject, and it is meant for @Output; using it for service messaging works but is discouraged. output() is only valid in components and directives, since it is tied to their lifetime. In a service, use a private Subject with asObservable(), or a signal.
ErrorHandler vs an HTTP error interceptor: which handles what?

An interceptor handles expected HTTP failures: it sees the status code, can retry idempotent calls, refresh a token on 401, redirect on 403, and convert a Spring ProblemDetail into a message. ErrorHandler is the last resort for unexpected bugs, such as a TypeError in a template; it should report and notify, not recover. If an HTTP error is not caught anywhere, it eventually reaches ErrorHandler too. 💡 Avoid showing two toasts for one failure by deciding where each kind of error is displayed.
How do you use httpResource / resource, and when would you still use HttpClient with RxJS?

httpResource(() => `/api/patients/${id()}`) creates a request that re-runs whenever the signals it reads change, and exposes value(), isLoading(), error() and reload() as signals. A previous request is cancelled when the inputs change, so it behaves like switchMap. It suits reads driven by component state. Use HttpClient directly for writes (POST/PUT/DELETE), and RxJS for complex flows such as debounce plus retry plus polling. These APIs were experimental when introduced, so check the version before relying on details.
PathLocationStrategy vs HashLocationStrategy: which do you use and what does the server need?

The default path strategy gives clean URLs (/patients/42), but a refresh sends that path to the server, so the server must return index.html for unknown non-API paths (nginx try_files or a Spring forward controller). The hash strategy (provideRouter(routes, withHashLocation())) gives /#/patients/42; the server only ever sees /, so no rewrite is needed. Hash URLs are uglier and do not work with SSR, so use them only when you cannot configure the server.
How do you set page titles per route, and why does it matter?

Add title: 'Patients' to a route, or a resolver function for dynamic titles. For a common suffix such as "Patients | MyApp", provide a custom TitleStrategy that overrides updateTitle(). Titles help users with many tabs open, help screen reader users know the page changed, and help SEO when combined with SSR. The Meta service sets description and Open Graph tags.
Should production builds ship source maps?

Source maps let error monitoring tools turn minified stack traces into real file and line numbers. A common approach is to generate them ("sourceMap": { "scripts": true, "hidden": true } in angular.json), upload them to the monitoring tool during CI, and not deploy them publicly. "Hidden" source maps are generated without the sourceMappingURL comment, so browsers do not fetch them. Shipping them publicly exposes readable source code, which is usually not a disaster since front-end code is public anyway, but it should be a deliberate choice.
How does Angular work with a Content Security Policy (CSP)?

A strict CSP blocks inline scripts and inline styles unless they carry a nonce. Angular inserts component styles at runtime, so you give it the nonce: add ngCspNonce="{{random}}" on the root element (filled in by the server per request) or provide the CSP_NONCE token. The server sets the same value in Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'nonce-…'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'. Do not use eval-style code, and note that AOT means Angular itself does not need unsafe-eval.
When would you NOT split an Angular app into micro-frontends?

When one team, or a few teams with a shared release cycle, own the app. Micro-frontends add runtime loading, shared dependency version management, duplicated styles, cross-app routing and harder end-to-end testing. A monorepo with lazy-loaded feature libraries and enforced module boundaries (for example Nx tags) gives most of the code-ownership benefit with one build. Choose micro-frontends when teams truly need independent deployment or must combine different frameworks.
How do you make a custom dropdown or modal accessible?

Prefer native elements (<select>, <dialog>) or a tested library such as Angular Material or CDK. If you build one: give it the right role (role="listbox", role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby), support keyboard (Escape closes, arrow keys move, Enter selects), trap focus inside a modal with cdkTrapFocus, and return focus to the trigger button on close. Reflect state with [attr.aria-expanded] and aria-activedescendant.
